# relnote

> Offline stdlib Python changelog CLI and GitHub Action for conventional-commit release notes.

relnote reads the current repository from the latest tag (or --since) to HEAD and prints a GitHub Release body grouped as Features (feat), Fixes (fix), Breaking (type! or BREAKING CHANGE:), and Other. Merge commits are omitted by default. No GitHub API, no config file, no third-party packages. Python 3.11+ and git on PATH.

It is a small git-cliff alternative when you want a Release body rather than a templated CHANGELOG.md (full guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/git-cliff-alternative.html). It is a gh release create --generate-notes alternative when you want offline notes grouped by commit type instead of official PR-linked notes.

It does not create the Release or the tag. Since v0.3.0, --next-version prints the next semver tag (breaking → major, feat → minor, else patch; 0.x breaking → minor), and --path DIR / --tag-prefix PREFIX scope notes and versions to one package in a monorepo. Since v0.2.0, --changelog CHANGELOG.md prepends a Keep a Changelog style "## [TITLE] - DATE" section for the new release (older entries untouched; duplicate titles refused). Since v0.3.5, with a github.com origin, (#41) squash-merge references in CHANGELOG.md bullets become pull request links.

## GitHub Action

loki-inu/relnote@v0.3.7 after actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0. The notes output is the Release body. Outputs: notes, next-version, has-changes. With no new commits (e.g. an untouched monorepo package) the step succeeds with has-changes=false and empty notes (fail-on-empty: true restores the old failure). chore(release) commits are left out of notes by default (--include-release-commits / include-release-commits: true keeps them). On a tag push (HEAD is the new tag) the range runs from the previous tag to the pushed tag, and from v0.3.4 the compare link ends at that tag instead of HEAD. Pass outputs to run: scripts via env:, not inline ${{ }} (notes contain backticks). Guide (tag-push draft Release, has-changes gated release button, monorepo matrix, CHANGELOG.md, inputs/outputs table): https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/github-action.html. CI can also run: relnote --output notes.md --quiet

## GitLab CI, Jenkins, Buildkite, CircleCI

Download the single file in the job and run it; the clone must have full history and tags (GitLab: GIT_DEPTH: 0). GitLab example: a tag-pipeline job in python:3.12 writes notes.md as an artifact, and a job in registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:latest publishes it with the release keyword (description: notes.md) or glab release create TAG --notes-file notes.md. A manual or scheduled job can use --next-version to pick the tag. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/ci.html

## standard-version alternative

standard-version is deprecated. examples/release.sh (bash, in the relnote repo) replaces npx standard-version locally: relnote --next-version (or --release-as TAG), --bump-file package.json/pyproject.toml/Cargo.toml (first version line), relnote --changelog CHANGELOG.md, commit chore(release): vX.Y.Z, annotated tag. --dry-run, --skip-commit, --skip-tag, --tag-prefix, --exec CMD (v0.3.7+, e.g. cargo update --workspace; changed tracked files are committed); nothing pushed. No prerelease bumps or .versionrc (use commit-and-tag-version for those). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/standard-version-alternative.html

## release-please alternative

No release PR bot: a workflow_dispatch job runs the relnote action (has-changes gate), then examples/release.sh --bump-file pyproject.toml (next version, version bump, CHANGELOG.md, chore(release) commit, annotated tag), pushes the commit and tag, and publishes relnote output with gh release create. From v0.3.6 the CHANGELOG.md compare link ends at the --changelog-title tag (e.g. v1.4.0) when HEAD is not tagged yet. Keep release-please for reviewed release PRs, per-language version updaters, or a protected main without a bypass token. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/release-please-alternative.html

## semantic-release alternative (no npm/Node)

Replace semantic-release's Node plugin stack with offline relnote + examples/release.sh + a workflow_dispatch (or tag-push) Actions job: has-changes gate, curl the pinned zipapp and release.sh (no npm for the tooling), --bump-file pyproject.toml or package.json, CHANGELOG.md, chore(release) commit, annotated tag, gh release create with --notes-file. Optional --exec "npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --silent" only when the product is npm. Differs from release-please-alternative (no release PR angle) and standard-version-alternative (local one-command). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/semantic-release-alternative.html

## conventional-changelog / commitizen alternative

conventional-changelog (conventional-changelog-cli and conventional-changelog-* presets) writes CHANGELOG.md and stops. commitizen and cz-cli prompt for a conventional commit message; they do not bump or tag, and relnote does not prompt — commits are already conventional. The offline zipapp plus examples/release.sh (pinned v0.3.7) prepends CHANGELOG.md, optionally bumps a version file (--bump-file; omit it for changelog + commit + tag only), commits chore(release): vX.Y.Z, and creates an annotated tag. --dry-run writes nothing. chore(release) commits are skipped in the notes unless --include-release-commits. Optional workflow_dispatch job: has-changes gate, same release.sh, gh release create --notes-file (never interpolate notes in run:). Node remains appropriate for an npm product (optional --exec to refresh package-lock.json; see npm-package.html), not for the release tooling. Differs from standard-version / commit-and-tag-version (Node one-command; see standard-version-alternative), semantic-release-alternative (CI publish loop), and release-please-alternative (release pull request). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/conventional-changelog-alternative.html

## Python packages (pyproject.toml, PyPI)

Locally: examples/release.sh --bump-file pyproject.toml (first version = "..." line, so [project] or [tool.poetry]) → next version from commits, CHANGELOG.md section, chore(release) commit, annotated tag; git push --follow-tags. Tag-push workflow: check v$version == tag via tomllib, python -m build, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish with trusted publishing (environment pypi, id-token: write only on that job), then gh release create TAG dist/* --notes-file with the loki-inu/relnote action's notes. Dynamic versions (setuptools-scm, hatch-vcs): skip --bump-file; the tag is the version. __version__: importlib.metadata.version("pkg"). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/python-package.html

## Rust crates (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, crates.io)

Locally: examples/release.sh --bump-file Cargo.toml --exec "cargo update --workspace" (v0.3.7+; --exec runs after the bump and CHANGELOG.md, before the commit, and tracked files it changes such as Cargo.lock are committed; NEXT_VERSION is exported) → next version, Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock bump, CHANGELOG.md section, chore(release) commit, annotated tag. Without the lock sync, cargo publish --locked fails (Cargo.lock needs updating but --locked was passed). Tag-push workflow: check v$version == tag via cargo metadata --no-deps | jq, cargo test --locked, rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1 (trusted publishing; first version published by hand), cargo publish --locked, then gh release create with the loki-inu/relnote action's notes. Shared workspace version: [workspace.package] version in the root Cargo.toml. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/rust-crate.html

## npm packages (package.json, package-lock.json, npmjs)

Locally: examples/release.sh --bump-file package.json --exec "npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --silent" (v0.3.7+; --exec runs after the bump and CHANGELOG.md, before the commit, and tracked files it changes such as package-lock.json are committed; NEXT_VERSION is exported) → next version, package.json + package-lock.json bump, CHANGELOG.md section, chore(release) commit, annotated tag. Without the lock sync, package-lock.json keeps the old version under packages[""].version and the next npm install dirties the tree. Tag-push workflow: check v$version == tag via node -p require('./package.json').version, npm ci, npm test, npm publish with trusted publishing (environment release, id-token: write; first version published by hand), then gh release create with the loki-inu/relnote action's notes. Workspaces: bump the root or use --tag-prefix / --path per package as on the monorepo page. Yarn Berry: --exec "yarn install --mode=update-lockfile"; pnpm: --exec "pnpm install --lockfile-only". Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/npm-package.html

## Go modules (git tags, go.mod, pkg.go.dev)

The version is the git tag (vX.Y.Z), not a field in go.mod. Locally: python3 -m relnote --since v1.2.0 --until v1.3.0, or python3 -m relnote with no flags when HEAD is that tag (the range starts at the previous tag and the compare link ends at the tag). python3 -m relnote --next-version prints the next tag (breaking → major, feat → minor, else patch; 0.x breaking → minor) before you tag. For major version 2 or higher the module path must end in /vN (module github.com/you/demo/v2 for tag v2.0.0). A module in the repo root or in a major-version subdirectory v2/ is still tagged v2.0.0, not v2/v2.0.0. A module in some other subdirectory uses a tag prefix and --tag-prefix / --path (see monorepo.html). Tag-push workflow: actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0, loki-inu/relnote@v0.3.7, then gh release create --notes-file (notes passed through env). GoReleaser's documented flag is goreleaser release --release-notes=FILE (skips its own changelog). changelog.disable ignores that flag. If the GitHub Release already has body text, GoReleaser keeps it unless release.mode is replace. pkg.go.dev resolves the tag; the GitHub Release is the notes. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/go-module.html

## Release Drafter alternative

Release Drafter (release-drafter/release-drafter) drafts a GitHub Release from merged pull requests. The example config is .github/release-drafter.yml, which groups those pull requests by labels (feature, enhancement, bug, chore) or by a when.conventional title rule, and the action creates or updates the draft through the GitHub API (contents: write, pull-requests: read). Autolabeler is a separate action that applies labels. relnote is the offline alternative when commits already follow conventional commits: python3 -m relnote --output notes.md --quiet writes the Release body from git history, --next-version prints the next tag (breaking → major, feat → minor, else patch; 0.x breaking → minor), and --changelog CHANGELOG.md prepends one section and does not commit. No labels, no release-drafter.yml, and no token to generate the notes. Publish with the workflows on the GitHub Action guide: a tag-push draft (loki-inu/relnote@v0.3.7 and softprops/action-gh-release, or gh release create --draft with the notes in env) or a workflow_dispatch job that gates on has-changes and runs gh release create with next-version. Those jobs create a Release; they do not update a draft on every merge. Keep Release Drafter for label-based categories, that living draft, or Autolabeler. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/release-drafter-alternative.html

## auto-changelog alternative

auto-changelog (cookpete/auto-changelog, npm package auto-changelog) generates a changelog from git tags and commit history. The published version on npm is 2.7.0. That release's README requires git 1.7.2 or later and semver tags (what npm version creates by default), and the package engines field is node >= 10. auto-changelog writes CHANGELOG.md by default (--output overrides the path; --stdout prints it) using a Handlebars template: compact (default), keepachangelog, json, a local template file, or a URL passed on the command line. Options live in package.json under the auto-changelog key or in .auto-changelog; package.json takes precedence. In-repo config is untrusted: values that load code, fetch a template URL, or write outside the repository are refused unless you pass --unsafe-config. The default --commit-limit is 3 (--commit-limit false shows every commit; --backfill-limit defaults to 3). --breaking-pattern highlights matching commits and those ignore the limit; the README example is "BREAKING CHANGE:". The README describes the output as tagged versions, merged pull requests, and closed issues. Grouping by conventional type is a custom template via the commit-list helper, not the default. A documented package.json version script is auto-changelog -p && git add CHANGELOG.md; -p/--package uses the version in package.json as the latest release. It does not choose the next semver and it does not create a GitHub Release. Link targets cover GitHub, GitLab, BitBucket, and Azure DevOps. The repository default branch documents an unreleased v3 (git 2.16 or later, Node ^22.23 || ^24.20 || >= 25.9); npm install today is still 2.7.0. relnote is the offline alternative when commits already follow conventional commits: python3 -m relnote --output notes.md --quiet writes the Release body, --next-version prints the next tag (breaking → major, feat → minor, else patch; 0.x breaking → minor), and --changelog CHANGELOG.md prepends one section and does not commit. No Node package, no Handlebars template, no .auto-changelog, and no default cap of 3 commits. Publish with the workflows on the GitHub Action guide. Keep auto-changelog to rebuild CHANGELOG.md from semver tags, to stay on the npm version hook, for Handlebars templates, or for GitLab, BitBucket, and Azure DevOps links. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/auto-changelog-alternative.html

## github-changelog-generator alternative

github-changelog-generator (github-changelog-generator/github-changelog-generator, Ruby gem github_changelog_generator) rebuilds CHANGELOG.md from GitHub tags, closed issues, and merged pull requests. The published gem is 1.18.0. The 1.18.0 gemspec requires Ruby >= 3.0. Install is gem install github_changelog_generator; the executable is github_changelog_generator --user USER --project PROJECT. It fetches tags, issues, and pull requests through the GitHub API (Octokit). It does not read the local commit log. The README says GitHub allows 50 unauthenticated requests per hour. The --token help says a token is required to make more than 50 requests per hour: pass --token or set CHANGELOG_GITHUB_TOKEN. The README says a private repository needs that token with the repo scope. Default output is CHANGELOG.md, and the file is overwritten. If HISTORY.md exists it is appended (the default of --base). Sections come from labels (parser defaults include enhancement, bug, breaking, plus closed issues and merged pull requests). Exclude labels include question, duplicate, invalid, and wontfix. Options can live in .github_changelog_generator; command-line options are applied again after the file. --future-release names the unreleased section and does not compute the next semver. --unreleased defaults to true. --since-tag starts after a tag. --github-site and --github-api target GitHub Enterprise. A Rake task, GitHubChangelogGenerator::RakeTask, takes the same options. The gem does not create the GitHub Release; the README then shows gh release create --notes-file. relnote is the offline alternative when commits already follow conventional commits: python3 -m relnote --output notes.md --quiet writes the Release body from git history, --next-version prints the next tag (breaking → major, feat → minor, else patch; 0.x breaking → minor), and --changelog CHANGELOG.md prepends one section and does not commit. No Ruby gem, no .github_changelog_generator, and no token to generate the notes. Publish with the workflows on the GitHub Action guide. Keep github-changelog-generator to rebuild CHANGELOG.md from GitHub issues and pull requests, for label sections, or for GitHub Enterprise. Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/github-changelog-generator-alternative.html

## towncrier alternative

towncrier (twisted/towncrier, PyPI package towncrier) builds a news file from news fragments instead of reading Git history. This page quotes the Towncrier 26.9.0 documentation (tutorial, command line reference, and configuration reference). The 26.9.0 homepage says it is used by Twisted, pytest, pip, BuildBot, and attrs, among others. The command line tool requires Python. The same page says it is usable with any project type on any platform if you do not use Python-specific affordances such as auto-detection of the project version. Install in the tutorial is python3 -m pip install towncrier. Config lives in towncrier.toml or pyproject.toml under [tool.towncrier]. If both exist, towncrier.toml takes precedence. --config selects another file. The default fragment directory is newsfragments (inside the package when package is set). The default filename is NEWS.rst. A fragment name is an issue id, a type, and an optional suffix, such as 1234.bugfix or 3456.doc.rst. towncrier create writes one. An orphan fragment starts with +. The default types are feature, bugfix, doc, removal, and misc. The tutorial says misc does not put the file contents in the news file. towncrier build is the default command. Processed fragments are removed by default (git rm for committed fragments). --keep leaves them. --yes skips confirmation. --draft prints to stdout and does not write files. The tutorial's production step stages the news file with git add and leaves the commit to you. New notes go after the start string (.. towncrier release notes start, or the HTML comment when filename ends with .md). If there are no fragments, a notice of "no significant changes" is added. Version comes from --version, then the version key, then for a Python package the installed metadata or __version__. It does not compute the next tag from commits. --date sets YYYY-MM-DD. towncrier check requires a fragment on a feature branch (skipped when the news file itself changes; default compare origin/main, fallback origin/master). relnote is the offline alternative when commits already follow conventional commits and you do not want a fragment file per change: python3 -m relnote --output notes.md --quiet writes the Release body from git history, --next-version prints the next tag (breaking → major, feat → minor, else patch; 0.x breaking → minor), and --changelog CHANGELOG.md prepends one section and does not commit. No newsfragments directory, no towncrier.toml, and no [tool.towncrier] table. The CI form is loki-inu/relnote@v0.3.7 after checkout with fetch-depth: 0. Publish with the workflows on the GitHub Action guide. Keep towncrier for curated per-change fragments, towncrier check, or the Python package integration (package version, newsfragments, pyproject.toml). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/towncrier-alternative.html

## git-cliff alternative

git-cliff (oratorio-rs/git-cliff) is a Rust binary with cliff.toml and Tera templates that rebuild CHANGELOG.md from history. relnote is the offline stdlib Python zipapp alternative when you want a GitHub Release body from conventional commits, one Keep a Changelog section prepended per release (older entries untouched), and optional next-version / bump / commit / tag via examples/release.sh — no cliff.toml, no cargo install, no template language. Pin curl and loki-inu/relnote@v0.3.7. Optional workflow_dispatch: has-changes gate, same release.sh, gh release create --notes-file (never interpolate notes in run:). Keep git-cliff for full-history rebuild, custom Tera templates, commit parsers, or remote contributor metadata. Differs from conventional-changelog-alternative (Node plugins / commitizen prompts) and changelog.html (--changelog flag detail). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/git-cliff-alternative.html

## Compared to nearby tools

- git-cliff: keep it for templated CHANGELOG.md rebuilt from history and version bump. relnote prints a Release body, can prepend one release to CHANGELOG.md, and needs no config. Full page: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/git-cliff-alternative.html
- gh release create --generate-notes: keep it for official PR-linked notes. relnote runs offline and groups by conventional-commit type.
- swapnanil/relnotes: another stdlib Python conventional-commit notes CLI. Pick relnote for the GitHub Action, --quiet/--output CI, and bot or secret-looking subject filters. Pick that CLI for optional .relnotes.toml, inferred semver bump, or --from/--to.

## Install

Single file (Python zipapp attached to each GitHub Release; needs Python 3.11+ and git, nothing else). Guide: https://loki-inu.github.io/relnote/single-file.html
curl -fsSL -o ~/.local/bin/relnote https://github.com/loki-inu/relnote/releases/latest/download/relnote && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/relnote
Pin a version with releases/download/v0.3.7/relnote. The release also has SHA256SUMS and relnote.pyz (same bytes, for python relnote.pyz on Windows).

pip install git+https://github.com/loki-inu/relnote.git
relnote --help

Or from a checkout: python3 -m relnote

Homebrew (macOS or Linux): brew install loki-inu/tap/relnote (tap: https://github.com/loki-inu/homebrew-tap)
conda-forge (any OS): pixi global install relnote, or conda install -c conda-forge relnote (https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/relnote)

## GitHub CLI extension

gh extension install loki-inu/gh-relnote
gh relnote prints the notes; gh relnote create TAG [gh release create flags] [-- relnote flags] creates the Release with them. Bundles relnote, needs gh, git, Python 3.11+.
